title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous page): X̂ is a smooth complete curve over C, D is a reduced divisor of ν points, and X = X̂ − D. Grothendieck studies the space of projective connections (projective structures, Schwarzian-type operators) on X that are 'regular at infinity'. Two such connections differ by a quadratic differential, so this space is a torsor under H^0(X, ω^2)^reg. From the context of the previous page, which computes the dual of Q(X) and the sequence 0 → H^0(X̂, ω²) → H^0(X̂, ω²(D)) → H^0(D, ω(D)) → Q̌(X) → 0, 'reg' means H^0(X̂, ω^2(D)): quadratic differentials with at most simple poles at the punctures.

Genus 0 (X̂ = P^1): deg ω²(D) = ν − 4, so h^0 = max(0, ν − 3).
- For ν ≤ 3 the group is 0. Hence there is exactly one regular projective connection on X: the restriction of the unique projective structure on P^1.
- For ν ≥ 4 the dimension is ν − 3 = dim M_{0,ν}. Grothendieck conjectures a canonical isomorphism H^0(X, ω²)^reg ≅ Ω^1_{M_{0,ν}}(s), the cotangent fibre of the moduli space at the point s = [X]. This is the Kodaira–Spencer / Serre-duality identification T*_s M_{0,ν} = H^0(P^1, ω²(D)).

He stresses that the unique structure for ν ≤ 3 is purely algebraic ('n'a rien de transcendant'). It is given in 'oper' form as P_X = X̂ × X → X: the trivial P^1-bundle with the diagonal section, which is transversal to the trivial connection. For arbitrary genus-0 X this connection is still defined. It therefore gives a canonical algebraic section of the affine bundle (torsor under the cotangent bundle) of regular projective connections over M_{0,ν}.

The purpose is to understand the torsor of projective connections over moduli, and its canonical sections, as part of the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs project. The next page treats the analogous problem for torsors under 1-dimensional group schemes, in any characteristic with 2 invertible, via 2-jets and a canonical Campbell–Hausdorff section.
errors: No real error. One implicit point: 'reg' must mean 'difference with at most simple poles' (i.e. ω²(D)) for the dimension count ν−3 to hold. With that convention the Fuchsian/uniformizing projective structure (double poles with coefficient 1/2) is NOT in this torsor. It lies in a parallel torsor under the same vector space, so 'unique for ν≤3' refers to Grothendieck's class, not to the uniformizing structure.
The isomorphism with Ω^1_{M_{0,ν}}(s) is stated only as a guess ('sans doute'); no argument is given. It is correct by standard deformation theory.

ideas.what: Projective connections on a punctured curve form a torsor under quadratic differentials with simple poles, of dimension ν−3 in genus 0, identified with the cotangent space of M_{0,ν}
ideas.modern_name: affine bundle of projective structures over moduli space, modelled on T*M_{g,n}; accessory parameters
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Poincaré/Klein accessory parameters); modern form Gunning, Hubbard, Kawai, Takhtajan–Zograf

ideas.what: Projective connection described as a P^1-bundle with a transversal section and a flat connection (P_X = X̂×X, diagonal section, trivial connection)
Genus-0 restriction of the projective structure on P^1 gives a canonical algebraic section of the torsor of projective structures over M_{0,ν}
ideas.modern_name: canonical (Schottky/genus-0) reference section; Fuchsian section minus this = accessory-parameter 1-form

missed.claim: Around 1972, in an algebraic setting, Grothendieck sets up the torsor of projective connections over M_{0,ν} and observes that it has a canonical algebraic section. This is the reference section later used by Takhtajan–Zograf, whose difference with the Fuchsian section gives the accessory parameters, whose antiholomorphic derivative is the Weil–Petersson form. He does not reach the uniformization comparison here, but he frames it in oper language over a general base.
missed.quote: sans doute on trouvera même un isom can $H^0(X,\underline{\omega}^2)^{reg}\simeq\Omega^1_{M_{0,\nu}}(s)$ ... cette connexion projective est ... définie, et fournit une section canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority note for the indigenous-bundle/oper viewpoint on moduli (pre-Mochizuki, pre-Beilinson–Drinfeld). It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard deformation theory plus classical accessory-parameter dimension counts. The early algebraic 'oper' formulation and the canonical section over M_{0,ν} are of mild historical interest.
